fields.features_heading: Inside a Marketing Quiz Built on Emergent
fields.features_subheading: A marketing quiz checks what someone knows about pricing and ad math. Emergent builds the quiz and its answer table.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted from one chapter

Name a chapter, such as pricing, or paste your notes, and Emergent drafts each question with one right answer and three wrong ones of the same kind. A prompt rewrites any of them.
fields.feature_2:
A reason under every answer

When the quiz ends, each question shows the right answer and a one-line reason with its source. You set the score bands, such as 0 to 3 out of 8, and a next step for each band.
fields.feature_3:
The wrong option each person chose

Every answer is a row in a database you own, with the person, the question, and the option chosen. Count the wrong options on one question to see which two ideas a class mixed up.
fields.feature_4:
Taken on a phone, one question at a time

Learners answer one question per screen on a phone, with a progress bar above it. A new coordinator can finish a 12-question quiz on the train before the first client call.
fields.feature_5:
A Slack message below the pass mark

Set a pass mark, and the app sends a Slack message or an email when someone scores below it. Instructors can get a Friday email with the class average and the question missed most.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, with the code in GitHub

Host the quiz on your own domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and run the quiz next term.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Groups Use a Marketing Quiz
fields.tab_content_1:
Skimming or penetration pricing: 51 of 118 picked wrong

After the pricing chapter, the 118 students in MKT 110 at Sedgefield Community College take a 10-question quiz. Each answer is saved with the option the student chose. On the price skimming question, 51 of 118 picked penetration pricing. The instructor taught the two side by side in Thursday's class.
fields.tab_content_2:
Nadia learns in Slack which 2 coordinators fell short

Corvale Digital hires account coordinators in groups, and each one takes a 12-question quiz on reporting terms, such as CTR and conversion rate, in week 1. The pass mark is 10 of 12. Of the 7 hired in March, 2 scored below it, and onboarding lead Nadia Lofthouse got a Slack message with both names and scores.
fields.tab_content_3:
Shop owners went from 3.5 to 6.2, and segmentation lagged

Thirty-six shop owners at a Tillmore Chamber of Commerce workshop answer the same 8 questions at the start and at the end. Their average rose from 3.5 at 9 a.m. to 6.2 of 8 at noon. Segmentation stayed lowest, with 14 of 36 right at noon. The next workshop adds an exercise on splitting a customer list.
fields.tab_content_4:
Northwick sends West reps to a refresher at 6.1 of 10

A week before launch, the 24 sales reps at Northwick Software take a 10-question quiz on the new Teams plan and how it differs from the Starter plan. A dashboard splits the scores by team. The East team of 15 averaged 8.4 of 10. The West team of 9 averaged 6.1 of 10 and got a 30-minute refresher before launch day.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Marketing Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write a marketing quiz whose wrong answers tell you which ideas a class or team confused.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Keep each quiz to one topic
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for a decision, not a definition
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Build wrong options from real mix-ups
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Add math with one exact answer
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name one topic per quiz, such as pricing or the marketing mix. Results from a single topic point at a single lesson. Put the topic and the course or team in your prompt, and Emergent drafts the questions around them.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Have learners apply a term instead of reciting it. Describe a launch with a high price that falls over time, then ask which strategy it is. A scenario shows whether someone can use the idea at work.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write wrong options from ideas people confuse, such as price skimming and penetration pricing, or CTR and conversion rate. Keep every option the same length and kind. A right answer longer or more precise than the rest gives itself away.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Include two or three questions with numbers, such as an ad shown 2,000 times that gets 50 clicks. Work each answer yourself first and put the working in the explanation. A learner who missed it can then follow every step.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Set the pass mark before launch
fields.howto_step_5_des: Choose the pass mark before anyone answers, such as 7 of 10 for a course. Write one line for each score band that says what to review next, and send any score under the mark to the person who teaches.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Run it past a colleague first
fields.howto_step_6_des: Have a colleague and one learner take the quiz before the group does. Look for a question where the two of them argue for different answers, and for an option neither considered. Rewrite both before launch.
fields.howto_step_7_des: When the quiz closes, count the wrong options chosen on each question. Open the next session with the mix-up the most people made, then test the same idea again in a new scenario on the next quiz.

faq_plan.a: A marketing quiz is a short, scored set of questions that tests how well someone knows marketing concepts, such as the 4 Ps or pricing strategies. Each question has one right answer. Run one after a course chapter, or in a new hire's first week, to see which concepts need more time.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a marketing quiz?
faq_plan.a: Pick one topic, write questions that ask learners to apply each term, and give every question one right answer and three believable wrong ones. With Emergent's AI survey builder, you describe the quiz in a prompt and get it with scoring and a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What topics should marketing quiz questions cover?
faq_plan.a: Cover the topics your course or team works with: the 4 Ps of the marketing mix (product, price, place, and promotion), segmentation, pricing strategies, and the ad metrics people report on, such as click-through rate. Spread the questions evenly, about two per topic in a 10-question quiz. The results then show which area needs the most work.

faq_plan.q: Should marketing quiz questions and answers include an explanation?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Show the right answer with a one-line reason after the quiz, and a wrong pick turns into a lesson instead of a lost point. A marketing quiz scores each answer as right or wrong, unlike a style quiz, where each answer points toward a result with no wrong choice.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a marketing quiz have?
faq_plan.a: Use 8 to 12 questions for a quiz on one chapter or topic, short enough to finish in one sitting on a phone. A longer review before an exam can run 20 to 25 questions, split into one section per topic. Each section's score then stands on its own.

faq_plan.q: Can a marketing quiz help train new hires at an agency?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Give new hires a short quiz in their first week on the terms they will report on, such as conversion rate, and set a pass mark. Anyone below it gets time with a lead before working on client reports. On Emergent, the quiz can send a Slack or email alert when someone scores under the pass mark.

faq_plan.q: How do I make a marketing terms quiz for students?
faq_plan.a: List the terms from the chapter, write a plain definition for each, and ask both ways: show the term and ask for its meaning, or describe it in use and ask for the term. It works like a vocabulary quiz for marketing, with scenario questions added that make students apply each term.

faq_plan.q: How do I grade a marketing quiz automatically?
faq_plan.a: Mark one option correct for each question and set score bands, and the quiz counts the right answers when someone submits. In a quiz built on Emergent, each answer is stored with the person and the question in a database you own. Sort it by person for scores, or by question to see what the group missed.

faq_plan.q: How do I compare marketing quiz scores before and after a workshop?
faq_plan.a: Ask identical questions when the session opens and when it closes, and match each person's two scores by name or email. Compare the averages first, then each question on its own: a question that stays low at the close points to a topic the session did not land. Change a question, and the comparison breaks.

faq_plan.q: What is the difference between a marketing quiz and a marketing survey?
faq_plan.a: A marketing quiz has right answers and a score; a marketing survey has no right answers and collects opinions instead. Use a quiz to test what people know about marketing. To learn what customers think, run a survey, such as a product market fit survey that asks how they would feel if your product went away.

quiz.title: Marketing Quiz: 8 Questions on the Basics
quiz.intro: Eight questions on the marketing mix, pricing, segmentation, and ad math. Pick one answer each; your score and the reason behind every answer show at the end.

questions.text: The American Marketing Association defines marketing as creating, communicating, delivering, and exchanging what?
questions.explanation: The definition puts value first: offerings that have value for customers, clients, partners, and society at large.

source.quote: creating, communicating, delivering, and exchanging offerings that have value for customers, clients, partners, and society at large

questions.text: The marketing mix is often called the 4 Ps. Which four?
questions.explanation: Product, price, place, and promotion are the four categories the parts of the marketing mix are sorted into.

source.quote: sometimes sorted into the categories of product, price, place, and promotion

questions.text: A company splits its customers into groups by age and buying habits. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Segmentation divides a market into meaningful sub-groups, called segments, so each one can get its own marketing.

source.quote: market segmentation or customer segmentation is the process of dividing a consumer or business market into meaningful sub-groups

questions.text: A new game console launches at a high price that drops later as early demand runs out. Which strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Skimming starts high for the buyers who want the product most, then lowers the price for the next group of buyers.

source.quote: Price skimming is a price strategy where a marketer initially offers an item at a high price

questions.text: A meal kit launches at a low price to reach a wide share of the market fast. Which strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Penetration pricing is the opposite of skimming: the launch price is set low to reach a wide fraction of the market quickly.

source.quote: Penetration pricing is a pricing strategy especially appropriate for new product pricing, where the price of a product is initially set low to rapidly reach a wide fraction of the market

questions.text: An ad is shown 2,000 times and gets 50 clicks. What is its click-through rate?
questions.explanation: Click-through rate is clicks divided by the times the ad is shown: 50 divided by 2,000 is 0.025, or 2.5%.

source.quote: CTR is the number of clicks that your ad receives divided by the number of times your ad is shown

questions.text: An ad gets 400 clicks, and 18 of those visitors sign up. What is the conversion rate?
questions.explanation: Conversion rate is conversions divided by ad interactions, here clicks: 18 divided by 400 is 0.045, or 4.5%.

source.quote: taking the number of conversions and dividing that by the number of total ad interactions

questions.text: A shop spends $3,000 on ads in a month and wins 60 new customers. What did each new customer cost to acquire?
questions.explanation: Customer acquisition cost is what it takes to win one customer: $3,000 divided by 60 new customers is $50 each.

source.quote: is the cost of persuading a customer to purchase a product or service
